science.title: Stratospheric Balloon Telescope Peeks Above The Clouds At The Sun
science.description: There’s lots of things you can do with balloons. Children’s birthday parties come to mind, as do retirement parties. But you can also observe the Sun in unprecedented detail with one - or at least with a suite of equipment attached to a gondola floating beneath one. That’s what the SUNRISE III mission did back in 2024, and scientists have had time to compile a series of three scientific papers on the results from that mission, which have been published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

science.title: A photoinduced, FeX3-catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MXn via a radical-polar crossover reaction
science.description: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. The goal of chemists is to establish green, inherently safe, highly efficient and sustainable synthetic methods. Here, we report a green approach for the halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn and FeX3, as well as a nucleophile at room temperature under visible-light irradiation in AcOH/CH3CN, without strong oxidants and any ligand. This procedure provides a wide substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, ranging from alkenes and conjugated dienes to medicinally active fragments. The reaction results in good to excellent yields, such as 82% and 84% for the bromoalcoholization and chlorobromination of cyclohexene, respectively. The method exhibits high stereoselectivity, regioselectivity and chemoselectivity, and mechanistic studies support the hypothesis that the reaction is a cascade process based on radical-polar crossover species, supported by DFT calculations. The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. Here, the authors report the FeX3-catalyzed halofunctionalization of alkenes with MXn at room temperature, under visible-light irradiation, and without strong oxidants.

science.title: Hybrid quantum computer observes foundational quantum effect in a new setting
science.description: Physicists in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford have used a hybrid quantum computer, made up of qubits and quantum oscillators, to observe the Aharonov–Bohm effect in a quantum simulation. The effect is a quantum phenomenon in which a particle can acquire a measurable phase by traveling around a magnetic flux, even though it never passes through a region where a magnetic field is present.
